header.stance: 通膨仍黏著，聯準會再次升息尚未排除

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 通膨仍限制聯準會的選擇，美債回吐部分漲幅

7月通膨數據公布後，美債小幅走弱。消費降溫、油價續跌，仍不足以讓市場排除聯準會再次升息的可能。2年、5年與10年期殖利率各上升2個基點，收在4.19%、4.37%及4.66%；30年期上升1個基點至5.18%。10年期殖利率的漲幅全數來自實質殖利率，後者升至2.34%，損益兩平通膨率則維持2.32%。

7月核心PCE月增0.2%、年增3.3%，均符合預期。實質消費持平、新屋銷售大減，提供聯準會繼續觀望的理由；但前期通膨上修、家庭所得回升，也讓進一步緊縮仍有依據。市場估計9月升息機率為43%，並已完全反映12月前升息25個基點，接下來將聽取Warsh在8月28日傑克森洞會議上的說法。

伊朗與阿曼就荷姆茲海峽水域及收益分配達成協議，帶動油價續跌，但伊朗強調這不代表海峽立即重啟。布蘭特原油下跌2.31%至$86.53，WTI下跌0.63%至$81.84。歐洲天然氣供應吃緊、日本運費急升，仍是央行難以忽視的通膨壓力。Schnabel主張歐洲央行進一步緊縮，日本服務價格數據也支持市場對9月升息的預期。

整體風險資產波動不大，S&P 500下跌0.02%，投資級債券ETF LQD下跌0.07%，主要高收益債ETF約跌0.02%。軟銀卻明顯承壓：市場傳出公司可能在境外發債$100億至$200億，一檔美元債價格下跌2.3美分，5年期CDS走寬10.7個基點。困境債方面，Brightline取得附帶破產聲請條件的新融資協議，Altice與Braskem債權人則持續爭取資產、參與權及清償順位。

## 消費降溫較明確，通膨改善仍有限

核心PCE月增幅雖然溫和，細項卻沒有同樣令人放心。扣除能源與住房後的服務價格上漲0.3%，其中投資組合管理及投資顧問費用上漲5.6%，為一年來最大漲幅；近期通膨數據也小幅上修。整體PCE年增率仍達3.7%，與核心指標一樣，明顯高於聯準會2%的目標。

實質消費在5、6月強勁成長後停滯。核心商品支出下滑0.8%，部分與亞馬遜將Prime Day從7月提前至6月有關；交通、餐飲與住宿則帶動實質服務支出增加0.3%。家庭可支配資源並未同步惡化：實質可支配所得增加0.4%，為1月以來最大增幅，儲蓄率也升至四個月高點3%。因此，這次支出放緩同時伴隨所得與儲蓄回補，尚非購買力突然大幅衰退。

房市的疲弱更為明顯。新屋銷售減少10.5%，年率降至60.7萬戶，低於市場預估的62萬戶，也低於前期修正後的67.8萬戶。新屋價格中位數已跌至五年低點，建商持續提供優惠，簽約量卻仍降至六個月低點。房貸利率、建築成本與前景不確定性，繼續壓抑這個近年由新屋承擔較高交易比重的市場。

里奇蒙聯準銀行調查呈現分歧。製造業指數由5降至4，不及預估的7，但出貨指數由8升至11；服務業營收指數則由−3降至−8。這些資料補強需求降溫的跡象，還不能視為各產業全面收縮。

即使週三殖利率回升，2年期仍較一個月前低14個基點。曲線變化不大，2s10s維持47個基點，2s30s收窄1個基點至99。美元指數隨實質殖利率上升而走高0.21%，黃金也上漲0.85%至$4,677.70。債市只是小幅調整，Warsh究竟需要看到多少通膨改善，才願意排除再次升息，仍是市場等待釐清的問題。

## 原油回落，天然氣與運費壓力尚未解除

伊朗革命衛隊發言人Hossein Mohebbi表示，伊朗與阿曼已就荷姆茲海峽各自的水域及收益分配達成協議，比先前的臨時架構更進一步，協助油價連續第三個交易日下跌。不過，協議並未說明正常航運何時恢復，伊朗也明確提醒，不能期待海峽立即重啟。

歐洲天然氣價格仍接近五個月高點，冬季合約價格超過去年同期的兩倍；儲氣率僅63%，為2009年以來同期最低。天然氣占歐盟能源供應21%，英國約25%至35%。經荷姆茲海峽運送的LNG缺乏替代航線，戰略庫存又有限，緩衝能力不如石油。

歐洲央行執委Schnabel認為，現行利率恐不足以在中期內讓通膨回到目標，應在能源成本傳導至工資前進一步緊縮。需求也仍有支撐：歐元區GDP在停滯後於第2季成長0.4%，德國成長率上修，財政、國防與AI支出持續挹注經濟。7月通膨達2.9%，市場已接近完全反映存款利率再升25個基點至2.5%。

日本7月企業服務價格年增3.6%，為5月以來最快增速，前面三個月的數據也都上修。航線拉長推升成本，海運服務價格大漲67.4%，創1986年有資料以來紀錄；4月年增率則已從初值3%修正至3.6%。市場估計日本央行9月18日升息機率約80%，副總裁冰見野良三即將發表的談話，將進一步反映央行如何評估這些壓力。

泰國央行則連續第三次一致決議，將隔夜附買回利率維持在1%。第2季GDP成長1.9%，為東南亞六大經濟體中最弱；大型企業放款雖改善，中小企業信用條件仍緊。官員預期聖嬰現象會推升通膨至2027年第1季，之後再回落。他們認為現行政策已屬寬鬆，暫無升降息理由，也提醒再降息未必能有效帶動借貸。第2季核准投資案實際支出共฿2,550億，其中AI相關項目超過฿1,270億，投資高度集中，也說明成長動能為何尚未均勻擴散。

巴西8月上旬通膨年增率降至4.24%，低於預估的4.33%，並落在3%目標上下1.5個百分點的容許區間。物價月減0.4%，降幅大於預估的0.32%；一次性電費抵減使住房成本下降1.41%，機票降價則協助運輸價格下滑1%。2027年1月到期交換利率盤中最多下降2.6個基點。部分改善屬暫時性，加上選舉相關社會支出支撐需求，仍需審慎看待；但央行在連續第四次降息25個基點、將Selic降至14%後，確實獲得更多政策空間。

## 美債回購改變部位配置，各國財政風險仍有差異

摩根士丹利投資管理的Vishal Khanduja在財政部宣布擴大長債回購後，減碼5s30s曲線陡峭化部位。公告以來，該期限利差已收窄約10個基點。巴克萊估計，每年新增回購可達$640億，相當於目前20年與30年期發債量的約15%。Citadel Securities策略師Frank Flight也撤回7月的看空立場，理由是通膨資料改善、空頭部位擁擠。

下一個實質債務管理決策時點是11月4日季度再融資公告。德意志銀行、摩根士丹利與花旗策略師討論的可能方向，包括增加國庫券及短期票據、長債標售持平或縮減、擴大回購，甚至在較低機率情境下取消20年期券。Bessent已排除在此之前調整例行標售。回購仍須動用現金或新增借款；縮短發債年期可以降低投資人承接的存續期間，卻會增加日後再融資需求。

法國面對的財政壓力更為迫切。10年期殖利率近二十年來首次突破4%，相對德債利差達86個基點，接近2012年以來最寬收盤水準。公債約占GDP的117%，政府已懷疑能否將今年赤字從2025年的5.1%降至5%。總理Sébastien Lecornu打算在不增稅下推動結構性節支，但9月底預算案尚未提出，便已遭遇反對。如果國會無法在4月18日及5月2日總統選舉投票前通過預算，緊急融資法案可能再增加至少相當於GDP 0.5個百分點的赤字。接下來的信評檢視將由惠譽率先展開。

捷克國會推翻總統Petr Pavel的否決，放寬財政限制以支應創紀錄基建支出。原本將2027年中央政府赤字限制在Kč1,500億的規則被排除，官員目前預估赤字將高於今年的Kč3,100億、但低於Kč4,000億。廣義政府赤字預估占GDP 2.8%，仍低於歐盟3%上限；債務比約46%，空間也大於法國。不過，融資需求預期已推高殖利率，反對派提出的憲法挑戰，也為包含創紀錄零售發債的籌資計畫增添變數。

中國招商銀行準備發行至多CN¥20億、3年期DR001連結浮動利率債，將是首家使用這項隔夜附買回基準的本地商業銀行。中國進出口銀行已在8月稍早採用，部分銀行也開始將其用於貸款。人民銀行從7天期附買回轉向隔夜操作目標，有望使銀行資產與負債的定價更一致，在利差接近歷史低點之際改善政策傳導。

印尼央行總裁候選人Destry Damayanti向國會表示，加強與政府協調不會損及央行獨立性，利率決策仍將採取前瞻、預先因應的方式。此前Perry Warjiyo提前離任，總統Prabowo Subianto的姪子出任副總裁，央行職責也擴及成長與就業。印尼盾反應不大，10年期殖利率維持上升3個基點。若獲任命，她將在2026至2031年任期內，一面管理流動性、匯市干預及高利率SRBI工具的退場，一面面對政府8%的成長目標。

墨西哥CDS下降，並未消除現券的相對折價。5年期保障成本為80個基點，低於Sheinbaum在2024年10月就任時的120個基點；但美銀估計，其美元債利差仍比同評級主權債寬39個基點，價格約相當於比正式評級低1.5個級距。八年累計$1,300億的Pemex援助，讓公司債務從2016年高點GDP的9.3%降至4%，代價則是風險移向政府。穆迪5月已將墨西哥降至投資級最底一級，標普展望為負向。

## 軟銀境外發債規畫，立即反映在債券與CDS

軟銀正討論最快9月在美元及歐元市場發行$100億至$200億債券，用來償還部分OpenAI投資所需的$400億過橋貸款，並支應其他AI承諾。公司預計到10月對OpenAI的投資將接近$650億。若採上限規模，將成為今年亞洲發行人最大的境外債券交易，並填補估計超過$200億融資缺口的大部分。

其8.5%美元債下跌2.3美分至約98，為4月發行以來最大單日跌幅；5年期CDS走寬10.7個基點，幅度為一個多月來最大。軟銀表示正評估多種再融資方案，金額尚未決定，最終規模、幣別及期限仍待確認。

擬採用的144A架構將是十多年來首次，可引入美國機構投資人，讓買方不只限於先前¥1兆零售發債計畫所鎖定的日本家庭。另有一筆以OpenAI持股擔保的$100億保證金融資，但契約可能要求補繳現金擔保或提前還款。軟銀4月也曾發行$36億美元與歐元債，其中就包括目前承壓的10年期8.5%券。

其他亞洲企業也準備向國際市場籌資。花旗今年迄今已協助韓國客戶募集約$600億，並預期2026年韓企境外股債發行將創紀錄。先前公布的晶片與資料中心投資規畫，已說明資金需求的規模；相較之下，軟銀次級市場價格下跌，更直接顯示投資人對承諾龐大、需要持續融資的借款人，可能要求多少額外補償。

## Brightline爭取破產融資，Altice與Braskem債權人加緊整合

佛羅里達鐵路公司Brightline與Assured Guaranty達成協議，若聲請Chapter 11，可取得至少$3.5億新貸款，聲請最快可能在數週內提出。公司共有$55億債務，多數已在困境價格交易。協議尚未生效，Brightline仍可選擇其他庭內或庭外處理方式。

Invesco、Nuveen及First Eagle持有$22億最高順位債務，其中約$11億由Assured提供保證，條件變更須取得其同意。Redwood Capital、Aristeia Capital及Nut Tree Capital領銜的避險基金集團，則持有$11億次順位公司票據的多數；另約$20億為順位較低的市政債。若提供破產程序中的DIP融資，Assured可能取得優先償還權，並提高協商影響力，但既有債權人的回收率尚未定案。

Altice International的擔保債權人Arini、Silver Point、King Street、Sona、Diameter與Invesco已組成聯盟，Elliott也正討論加入；若成行，持有比例將達擔保債務約60%。成員準備提告，並爭取優於委員會外債權人的待遇。爭議涉及€50億、約$53億的集團內貸款，以及葡萄牙和多明尼加業務移出受契約限制集團等涉嫌違反條款的安排。Altice Financing主張，債權人未證明具備必要持有額或授權，因此違約通知無效；債權人不同意這項說法。

Braskem新公布的各券參與比例，進一步揭示$110億重整案需要爭取哪些支持。2081年到期次順位券約67%加入，4.5%的2028年券約60%；7.25%的2033年券與8.5%的2031年券均約58%。相較之下，5.875%的2050年券僅約30%，7.125%的2041年券僅約13%；規模最大的4.5% 2030年券，支持與未加入的比例幾乎各半。

總支持額為R$224億、約$43億，占受影響債務39.6%，足以啟動先前公布的90天程序，但距離法院核准所需的過半門檻仍有差距。銀行要求增加擔保品，遭Braskem拒絕。Petrobras、IG4 Capital或經核准第三方的新股本投入或出資保證，規模、形式及時點也尚未確定。如今各券立場更清楚，協商焦點已不只是整體支持率，而是如何讓不同到期日與順位的持有人接受同一方案。

## 先看Warsh如何評估通膨，再看各項融資定案

Warsh在8月28日發言時，面對的是核心通膨3.3%、實質消費持平的組合。他如何看待前期修正、家庭需求及供應成本的持續性，將影響市場是否把原本完全反映在12月前的升息進一步提前至9月。2至5年期殖利率對時點變動最為敏感。

能源方面，荷姆茲海峽實際通行量及歐洲庫存，才能顯示外交進展有多少轉化為供應改善。原油降價，尚未解除天然氣與運費對歐洲、日本政策前景的壓力。

較近的融資觀察重點是軟銀最終規模、期限及定價，財政部11月4日再融資公告則將釐清政府發債組合。Brightline仍待融資安排生效及決定是否聲請破產，Altice的債權爭議尚未解決，Braskem則須取得多數支持。這些未定條款，比整體信用市場的平靜更能決定各自債券接下來的走向。

overall_summary.headline: PCE後美債小跌，軟銀融資規畫壓低自家債券
overall_summary.session_narrative:
10年期實質殖利率升至2.34%，損益兩平通膨率維持2.32%。7月核心PCE月增0.2%、年增3.3%，符合預期；實質消費停滯，新屋銷售減少10.5%。Warsh將在8月28日發言，市場目前估計9月升息機率43%。

伊朗與阿曼就荷姆茲水域及收益達成協議，但未確認立即重啟航運。原油下跌，歐洲天然氣短缺、日本運費通膨仍有壓力。Schnabel支持進一步緊縮，泰國維持利率，巴西通膨則降溫。

財政部回購促使投資人調整美債部位。軟銀尋求更廣的境外買方，Brightline安排附帶破產聲請條件的新融資；Braskem各券參與比例，則揭示仍須爭取哪些債權人支持。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Treasuries give back some gains as inflation leaves the Fed little room

Treasuries slipped after July inflation data left another Federal Reserve increase in play, despite weaker spending and a further decline in oil. Two-, 5- and 10-year yields each rose 2 basis points to 4.19%, 4.37% and 4.66%; the 30-year added 1 basis point to 5.18%. Ten-year real yields accounted for the entire nominal increase, rising to 2.34%, while breakevens held at 2.32%.

Core PCE rose an expected 0.2% in July and 3.3% from a year earlier. Flat real consumption and a steep fall in new-home sales gave the Fed reasons to wait, but upward inflation revisions and firmer household income left the case for further tightening intact. Markets assigned a 43% probability to a September increase and fully priced 25 basis points by December, ahead of Kevin Warsh's August 28 Jackson Hole address.

Oil fell again after Iran and Oman agreed on waters and revenues in the Strait of Hormuz, though Iran said the arrangement did not mean an immediate reopening. Brent lost 2.31% to $86.53 and WTI 0.63% to $81.84. European gas shortages and sharply higher Japanese freight costs continued to trouble policymakers even as crude eased. Schnabel called for further ECB tightening; Japan's service-price data reinforced expectations of a September hike.

Broad markets were quiet: the S&P 500 slipped 0.02%, investment-grade bond fund LQD lost 0.07%, and the main high-yield funds fell about 0.02%. SoftBank was a conspicuous exception. A possible $10 billion–$20 billion offshore issue sent one of its dollar bonds down 2.3 cents and widened its 5-year CDS by 10.7 basis points. In distressed debt, Brightline secured an agreement for prospective bankruptcy financing, while Altice and Braskem creditors fought over assets, participation and repayment priority.

## PCE cools spending more convincingly than inflation

The detail of July PCE was less reassuring than the moderate monthly headline for core prices. Services excluding energy and housing rose 0.3%, with portfolio-management and investment-advice prices up 5.6%, the most in a year. Recent inflation readings were revised slightly higher. Headline PCE remained 3.7% above a year earlier, leaving both measures well above the Fed's 2% goal.

Real spending stalled after strong gains in May and June. Core-goods outlays fell 0.8%, partly reflecting Amazon's decision to move Prime Day from July to June, while real services spending rose 0.3% on transport, restaurants and accommodation. Households had more income available: real disposable income increased 0.4%, its strongest gain since January, and the saving rate reached a four-month high of 3%. The spending pause therefore came with some rebuilding of financial buffers rather than a sudden loss of purchasing power.

Housing was weaker. New-home sales dropped 10.5% to a 607,000 annual rate, below the 620,000 forecast and down from a revised 678,000. Median prices reached a five-year low, yet contract signings fell to their lowest in six months despite builders' incentives. High mortgage rates, construction costs and uncertainty continued to restrain a market in which new homes have accounted for an unusually large share of transactions.

Richmond Fed surveys were mixed. The manufacturing index eased to 4 from 5, missing the forecast of 7, but shipments improved to 11 from 8. Services revenues fell to −8 from −3. The releases added to the evidence of cooling demand without showing a uniform contraction.

Two-year yields remained 14 basis points below a month earlier even after Wednesday's rise. The curve barely changed: 2s10s stayed at 47 basis points and 2s30s narrowed 1 basis point to 99. A 0.21% gain in the Dollar Index accompanied higher real yields, while gold rose 0.85% to $4,677.70. The modest rates adjustment left considerable uncertainty over how much further inflation progress Warsh will require before ruling out another increase.

## Cheaper oil leaves gas and freight inflation unresolved

IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi said Iran and Oman had agreed on their respective shares of Hormuz waters and revenues, advancing the earlier interim framework. That helped oil fall for a third session. The agreement did not establish when normal vessel traffic would resume, however, and Iran explicitly warned against expecting an immediate reopening.

European gas prices were near five-month highs, with winter contracts costing more than twice their year-earlier level. Storage was only 63% full, the lowest for the season since 2009. Gas supplies 21% of the EU's energy and roughly 25%–35% of Britain's. LNG cargoes passing through Hormuz lack an alternative route, while limited strategic inventories leave less protection than in oil.

ECB Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel said current rates were unlikely to bring inflation back to target over the medium term and called for further tightening before energy costs fed into wages. Demand was holding up: euro-area GDP grew 0.4% in Q2 after stagnating, German growth was revised higher, and fiscal, defense and AI spending provided support. With July inflation at 2.9%, markets were close to fully pricing a 25-basis-point increase in the deposit rate to 2.5%.

Japan's corporate service prices rose 3.6% in July, the fastest since May, after upward revisions to the previous three months. Ocean-freight prices surged 67.4%, a record in data beginning in 1986, as longer routes increased costs. April's initial 3% reading now stands at 3.6%. Markets priced about an 80% chance of a September 18 BOJ hike; Deputy Governor Ryozo Himino's upcoming remarks will provide another indication of the bank's assessment.

Thailand instead held its one-day repo rate at 1% unanimously for a third meeting. Q2 growth of 1.9% was the weakest among six major Southeast Asian economies, and small businesses still faced tight credit even as large-company lending improved. Officials expected El Nino to lift inflation through Q1 2027 before it subsided. They regarded current policy as accommodative, saw no immediate case for a move in either direction, and cautioned that additional cuts might do little for borrowing. More than 127 billion baht of the 255 billion baht spent on approved investment projects in Q2 was AI-related, a concentration that helps explain why investment strength had not spread evenly through the economy.

Brazil's early-August inflation fell to 4.24%, below the 4.33% forecast and within the 3% target's 1.5-percentage-point tolerance band. Monthly prices declined 0.4%, versus an expected 0.32% fall. A one-time electricity credit reduced housing costs 1.41%, and cheaper airfares helped transport prices fall 1%. January 2027 swaps declined as much as 2.6 basis points. Temporary relief and election-related social spending warrant caution, but the reading gave the central bank more room after its fourth consecutive 25-basis-point cut took Selic to 14%.

## Treasury buybacks change positioning as fiscal risks diverge abroad

Morgan Stanley Investment Management's Vishal Khanduja reduced a 5s30s steepener after Treasury announced larger long-bond buybacks. That gap had narrowed about 10 basis points since the announcement. Barclays estimated additional purchases of $64 billion a year, equivalent to roughly 15% of current 20- and 30-year supply. Citadel Securities strategist Frank Flight also reversed his July bearish call, citing improving inflation data and crowded short positions.

The next substantive debt-management decision comes at the November 4 refunding. Deutsche Bank, Morgan Stanley and Citigroup strategists have considered more bills and short notes, steady or smaller long-bond auctions, larger buybacks and, as a tail possibility, ending the 20-year maturity. Bessent has ruled out regular-auction changes before then. Repurchases still require cash or borrowing; issuing shorter debt would reduce the duration sold to investors while increasing future refinancing needs.

France faced a more immediate fiscal repricing. Its 10-year yield exceeded 4% for the first time in nearly two decades, and its German spread reached 86 basis points, near the widest closing level since 2012. Debt stands around 117% of GDP. The government already doubts it can lower this year's deficit to 5% from 5.1% in 2025, while Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu's plan for structural savings without new taxes faces opposition ahead of a late-September budget. Failure to secure a budget before the April 18 and May 2 presidential votes could require emergency funding legislation and add at least 0.5 percentage point of GDP to the deficit. Fitch opens the coming ratings-review calendar.

Czech lawmakers overrode President Petr Pavel's veto to loosen fiscal limits and permit record infrastructure spending. A rule that would have capped the 2027 central-government deficit at 150 billion koruna was set aside; officials now expect more than this year's 310 billion but less than 400 billion. General-government borrowing of 2.8% of GDP would remain below the EU's 3% ceiling, and debt near 46% leaves more room than France has. Yields have nevertheless risen with funding expectations. An opposition constitutional challenge complicates a program that also includes record retail issuance.

In China, Merchants Bank is preparing up to 2 billion yuan of 3-year floating-rate notes linked to overnight repo benchmark DR001, the first such issue from a domestic commercial bank. Export-Import Bank of China used it earlier in August, and lenders have begun referencing it in loans. The PBOC's shift from the 7-day repo toward an overnight operational target could align banks' asset and liability pricing more closely, improving policy transmission while margins hover near record lows.

Indonesia's prospective central-bank governor Destry Damayanti told parliament that closer government coordination would not compromise independence. She retained a preemptive, forward-looking approach to rates following Perry Warjiyo's early departure, the appointment of President Prabowo Subianto's nephew as a deputy governor, and a broader growth-and-employment mandate. The rupiah was little changed and the 10-year yield retained a 3-basis-point increase. Her proposed 2026–2031 term would include managing liquidity, intervention and a move away from high-yield SRBI securities alongside the government's 8% growth ambition.

Mexico's falling CDS masked a relative penalty in cash bonds. Five-year protection cost 80 basis points, down from 120 when Claudia Sheinbaum took office in October 2024. Bank of America nonetheless estimated dollar bonds traded 39 basis points wider than similarly rated sovereigns—about 1.5 rating notches below Mexico's formal standing. Eight years of $130 billion in Pemex support lowered the company's debt to 4% of GDP from a 2016 peak of 9.3%, but shifted risk onto the government. Moody's lowered Mexico to the bottom investment-grade tier in May; S&P's outlook is negative.

## SoftBank's offshore plan brings an immediate credit repricing

SoftBank is discussing a $10 billion–$20 billion dollar and euro bond sale, potentially in September, to repay part of its $40 billion OpenAI bridge loan and fund other AI commitments. Its OpenAI investment is scheduled to reach close to $65 billion by October. At the upper end, the sale would be Asia's largest offshore issue this year and cover much of a funding gap estimated above $20 billion.

Its 8.5% dollar bond fell 2.3 cents to about 98, the biggest daily decline since April issuance. Five-year CDS widened 10.7 basis points, the most in over a month. SoftBank said it was considering several refinancing options and had not decided the amount, leaving final size, currencies and maturities open.

The proposed 144A format, its first in more than a decade, would bring US institutional buyers into the financing. That expands the available investor base beyond the Japanese households targeted by its previously announced ¥1 trillion retail plan. A $10 billion margin loan secured by its OpenAI stake provides another source of funds, but covenants can require cash collateral or early repayment. SoftBank also sold $3.6 billion in dollar and euro debt in April, including the 10-year 8.5% bond now under pressure.

Other Asian companies are preparing to tap international capital. Citigroup expects record Korean overseas debt and equity issuance in 2026 after helping clients raise about $60 billion so far. Korea's previously reported chip and data-center investment plans explain the scale of demand, but SoftBank's secondary-market losses offered a more immediate measure of the price investors may require from a heavily committed borrower.

## Brightline seeks bankruptcy funding; Altice and Braskem creditors organize

Brightline agreed with Assured Guaranty on at least $350 million of new loans if the Florida railroad enters Chapter 11, potentially within weeks. The company has $5.5 billion of obligations, much of it trading at distressed prices. The agreement is not yet effective and Brightline can still pursue another in-court or out-of-court solution.

Assured guarantees about $1.1 billion of the $2.2 billion in highest-priority debt held by Invesco, Nuveen and First Eagle, and must consent to changes. Redwood Capital, Aristeia Capital and Nut Tree Capital lead a hedge-fund group holding a majority of $1.1 billion in junior corporate notes; roughly $2 billion more consists of lower-ranking municipal bonds. Providing debtor-in-possession financing could give Assured senior repayment rights and greater influence over negotiations, without yet settling recoveries for existing holders.

Altice International secured creditors Arini, Silver Point, King Street, Sona, Diameter and Invesco formed a bloc, with Elliott discussing membership. Its addition would bring the group to roughly 60% of secured debt. Members are prepared to litigate and seek better treatment than creditors outside the committee over alleged covenant breaches involving €5 billion, or $5.3 billion, of intercompany loans and transfers of the Portuguese and Dominican Republic businesses outside the restricted group. Altice Financing says the default notice is invalid because creditors failed to establish the necessary holdings or authority; creditors dispute that response.

Braskem's new series-level figures showed where it must win support for its $11 billion restructuring. About 67% of the subordinated 2081 notes joined, alongside roughly 60% of the 4.5% 2028s and 58% of both the 7.25% 2033s and 8.5% 2031s. Participation was only about 30% in the 5.875% 2050s and 13% in the 7.125% 2041s. The largest series, the 4.5% 2030s, was almost evenly divided.

Backing totaled 22.4 billion reais, or $4.3 billion and 39.6% of affected debt, enough to start the already-announced 90-day process but short of the majority required for court approval. Banks sought additional collateral that Braskem rejected. Fresh equity or a backstop from Petrobras, IG4 Capital or approved third parties remained unspecified in size, structure and timing. The instrument-level split now gives negotiations a clearer focus than the aggregate support figure alone.

## Warsh's inflation assessment comes before the funding decisions

Warsh's August 28 remarks will follow a report combining 3.3% core inflation with flat real spending. His assessment of revisions, household demand and the persistence of supply costs will matter for whether the increase fully priced by December moves closer to September. Two- to 5-year yields are most directly exposed to that change in timing.

For energy, actual Hormuz traffic and European storage will show how much of the diplomatic improvement reaches physical supply. Lower crude has not yet removed gas and freight pressures from the European and Japanese policy outlooks.

SoftBank's final size, maturities and pricing are nearer-term tests of financing capacity; Treasury's November 4 refunding will clarify the official supply mix. Brightline still needs an effective financing arrangement and a decision on filing, Altice faces contested creditor claims, and Braskem must assemble a majority. Those unresolved terms—not the calm in broad credit funds—will determine the next developments for their bondholders.
